name: Tree Traversals (Inorder/Preorder/Postorder)
description: Three fundamental depth-first traversal orders for binary trees: inorder (left-root-right), preorder (root-left-right), and postorder (left-right-root).
aim: Visit every node in a binary tree in a specific order to produce different useful sequences: sorted order (inorder on BST), copy order (preorder), or delete order (postorder).
howItWorks: Inorder: recurse left → visit root → recurse right (gives sorted order for BST)
Preorder: visit root → recurse left → recurse right (root before subtrees)
Postorder: recurse left → recurse right → visit root (children before parent)
All three have O(n) time since each node visited once

complexity.spaceDescription: Recursion stack depth = tree height h; O(log n) balanced, O(n) skewed

realWorld: Inorder: print BST in sorted order
Postorder: calculate size of directories (process children before parent)
whenToUse: Visiting all nodes in specific order
alternatives: Iterative with explicit stack — avoids recursion stack overflow
Morris traversal — O(1) space iterative traversal
